page: Microsoft Azure E96-24ads_v7 is a constrained-CPU memory-optimized virtual machine instance based on AMD EPYC 9V45 processors running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance features a 1:32 vCPU-to-memory ratio, providing 24 dedicated vCPUs (12 physical cores with 2 threads per core) clocked at up to 4.5 GHz alongside 768.0 GB of system memory. For high-throughput local IOPS and low latency requirements, the instance bundles a 5,669 GB local NVMe SSD array. The x86_64 architecture incorporates instruction set extensions including AVX-512 (with VNNI and BF16) and standard cryptographic acceleration modules.

Benchmark results highlight strong single-threaded CPU capability and memory characteristics. Stress-ng single-core performance reached 3,779.99, ranking in the top 10%, complemented by top-tier single-threaded gzip compression at 41.36 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 18.14 GB/sec. Uncached large-block read memory bandwidth achieves 103.44 GB/sec, while write bandwidth reaches 68.59 GB/sec. In LLM inference benchmarks utilizing small models (135M), text generation ranked in the top 10% at 458.89 tokens/sec, while prompt processing reached the top 25% at 3,179.89 tokens/sec. Conversely, multi-core metric outputs such as stress-ng multi-core (45,238.45) and PassMark CPU score (47,584.09) settle in the middle 50% due to the 24 vCPU limitation.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E96-24ads_v7 offers a distinct operational tradeoff. By constraining the active vCPU count to 24 while maintaining 768 GB of RAM and 5.6 TB of local NVMe storage, it targets workloads where per-core software licensing dominates total infrastructure expenditure. Rather than licensing the full 96 vCPUs typical of this chassis footprint, operators can reduce license overhead without sacrificing memory capacity or fast scratch storage.

The primary workload fit includes memory-intensive relational databases, large-scale in-memory caches, analytics engines, and transactional platforms that require large footprints of physical memory and fast temporary disk space but do not require wide core parallelization.
description: Microsoft Azure E96-24ads_v7 is a memory-optimized instance featuring 24 dedicated vCPUs (12 physical cores) powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at 4.5 GHz, paired with 768.0 GB of RAM. The instance incorporates 5,669 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and includes support for AVX-512 instruction extensions. Benchmark evaluations demonstrate top-tier single-core CPU throughput and decompression capabilities, alongside strong memory benchmark scores and top-tier small-model LLM generation speeds. Given the constrained 24 vCPU count on an otherwise high-memory footprint, it serves as a cost-efficient platform for workloads constrained by per-core software licensing. The instance is suited for in-memory databases, caching layers, and high-memory analytics processing that demand large memory density alongside fast local scratch space.
